Independent replay: python -B /workspace/branches/independent-reproductions.py 1; /workspace/branches/reproduction-1.out. Flux-derived symbolic nullspaces for k=1,…,6 and scaled trajectories for k=1,2,3 corroborate the proof. The k=1 sample at t=300 gives a resonant ratio of 1.0016844.
correctness.rationale: With N=2k in deficit coordinates, the reduced linearization is upper triangular with diagonal −(1−1/N),−1,…,−1. The positive left eigenvector normalized by c₁=1 has cⱼ=Ncⱼ₋₁+j. Consequently H=c·b is comparable to the mean deficit and |H′+(1−1/N)H|=O(H²). The convergence hypothesis and positivity give an eventual exponential bound from this scalar differential inequality alone, and integration of the logarithmic derivative then proves a finite strictly positive amplitude, not just an upper rate. Neither endpoint can be reached at finite time from a nonendpoint by ODE uniqueness, so both jump rates are positive on any finite interval and a positive mass propagates along each adjacent edge. The exact last-state identity (eᵗb_N)′=eᵗv(b_{N−1}+b_N) supplies positive B, finite when 2(1−1/N)>1. For d≥2 the other integrating factors have derivative eᵗb_{d+1} plus an integrable remainder; successive integrations give the claimed factorials and are o(e^{−(1−1/N)t}). If N=2, the preliminary decay gives b₂=o(e^{−t/2}); substitution into the last-state identity yields a derivative tending to C²/2 and a Cesàro limit. The reflected system has the same normalization. The attained-consensus assumption is essential and is not claimed to classify basins.
residual_risks: Finite simulations are diagnostics only. No finite-agent limit or full basin result is audited here.
